title: Abdominal Complaints in Low-Urgency Patients Presenting to a Statutory Emergency Practice – A Monocentric Cross-Sectional Observational Study
summary:
Despite extensive outpatient emergency care structures, the utilization of emergency departments (EDs) in Germany continues to rise, often driven by patients with low treatment urgency, leading to overcrowding and reduced quality of care. While decision-making processes for high-risk patients are well studied, there is a lack of evidence regarding patient-reported factors influencing referral from out-of-hours primary care services (KV emergency practices, NFP) to EDs, particularly among low-acuity patients presenting with abdominal complaints.
The aim of this study is to identify such predictors based on demographic characteristics, comorbidities, and symptom perception. The findings are intended to support the development of risk-adapted decision-making tools and to inform requirements for diagnostic infrastructure in outpatient emergency care, thereby improving cross-sectoral healthcare delivery.

interventions.name: Patients presenting with abdominal complaints in the emergency outpatient clinic fill out a questionaire regarding frequency, type, and duration of these abdominal symptoms.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- abdominal complaints as primary reason for consultation in an out of hours walk-in clinic
- Arrival without medical transport services (ambulatory/walk-in patients)
- Presentation to the out-of-hours walk-in clinic between 6:00 p.m. and 12:00 a.m. on weekdays or between 8:00 a.m. and 12:00 a.m. on weekends/public holidays
Exclusion criteria:
- Patient age < 18 years
- Patients not legally capable of giving informed consent
